gaps.sentence: She managed to ___ his attention during the whole lecture.
The new bridge ___ traffic congestion enormously.
gaps.explanation: The bridge is the agent: active present perfect — has reduced. 'Has been reduced' would mean someone reduced the bridge.

gaps.sentence: Her performance was ___ praised by the critics.
gaps.explanation: 'Widely praised/known/used' = by many people — fixed adverb collocation.

gaps.sentence: The scheme is ___ at reducing traffic in the centre.
gaps.explanation: 'Aimed at doing something' = intended to achieve it.

gaps.sentence: The meeting is ___ to last two hours.
gaps.explanation: 'Be expected to' = people think it will; 'wait' is not used this way in the passive.

gaps.sentence: The children were ___ by the fairy lights.
gaps.explanation: People are fascinated by things; things are fascinating.

gaps.sentence: The new timetable has caused a lot of ___ among commuters.
gaps.explanation: 'A lot of + noun' is needed: confusion. The others are verb/adjective forms.

gaps.sentence: She ___ a fortune by selling her flat at the right time.
gaps.explanation: 'Make a fortune / make money' is the collocation; 'gain' is not used with fortune this way.
